text:
Support: FYI customer acme-inc reports large spike of 5xx / timeouts against hosted inference endpoint in eu-west since ~09:12 UTC. happening across both chat & completion routes, high client impact. sending logs + repro.
Alex O.: oncall pinged. assigning triage. can someone grab telemetry? :eyes:
Support: repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
```
response: `502 Bad Gateway` + `upstream closed connection` and trace-id `trace:acme:eu:9a1b` in logs. Customer says errors ~25% of requests, p95 latency > 8s.
Maya CS: Customer on a paid Dedicated trial in eu-west but hitting the Hosted endpoint by mistake; they switched keys earlier today. we asked for full request ids. Customer needs ETA for restore, asking for fallback guidance to dedicated pool.
Sam (eng-sre): grabbing metrics now. seeing a concurrent spike in `apigw upstream 502` and `worker reconnects` starting 09:11:20. queue depth increased on the gateway by ~3x. I suspect transient KV-cache pressure + connection churn.

Jordan (eng-runtime): quick note: we rolled a kernel/quantize runtime config to eu-west 09:05 for a canary yesterday. rollout completed at 09:10 across edge nodes. could be related. adding `rollback` candidate.

Li (billing): ping — customer key used in hosted path, but they have a reserved Dedicated slot. billing shows no obvious quota hit. not billing-related atm.

Eve (oncall): I can put a mitigation window. proposed steps: 1) enable fallback to `redwood-7b` model variant for the customer route 2) temporarily route their API key to Dedicated pool 3) rollback runtime canary if correlated. Which step is lowest risk? :question:

Niaj (infra): routing their key to Dedicated is doable via the routing policy toggle (console or api) — will take ~3min to propagate. fallback to 7b is immediate via soft model mapping. Both are safe.

Alex O.: priority matrix: get customer back first (low friction). Niaj — route key to Dedicated now, Maya please confirm with customer when done. Sam & Jordan — investigate runtime rollout correlation. I'll take comms.

Support Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1745019999. War-room pinned. Related alerts: apigw-502-euwest, runtime-kernel-errors.

Sam (eng-sre): after quick checks: gateway error rate correlates to nodes reporting `kv-cache-evict-throttle` + `conn_reset_by_peer` on same hosts where new runtime landed. stack traces show `epoll` loop resets. collecting host ids.

Jordan (eng-runtime): found a mismatched socket option in the new kernel path for sequence long requests. plausible cause for resets under load. will prepare a rollback patch.

Alex O.: action owners summary (short):
- Niaj: route acme key -> Dedicated (now) — status?
- Maya CS: confirm with customer & ask them to retry traffic — status?
- Jordan: start rollback of runtime canary to previous build — status?
- Sam: gather host-level crash logs + postmortem notes for root cause — status?
- Li: confirm no billing/quotas impacted and log customer access change — status?
- Alex O.: own communication & postmortem writeup.

Niaj (infra): routing toggle applied at 09:18:24 UTC. propagation OK on control-plane logs. sample request now hitting Dedicated: `trace:acme:ded:9a1b`.

Maya CS: told customer at 09:19 UTC that we're routing them to Dedicated. customer retried 20 requests — 0 errors, p95 ~ 220ms. customer confirms reduced impact, very relieved. :relieved:

Support: customer provides one failing request id from before: `req_9a1b_0908` — attached stack trace snippet.

Sam (eng-sre): collected host logs from three affected hosts: `eu-west-node-112`, `eu-west-node-117`, `eu-west-node-121`. evidence of repeated `SOCKET_RESET` around 09:11–09:16. I'll upload artifact to the incident folder and start a timeline.

Jordan (eng-runtime): rolling back runtime canary now (09:24). patching nodes in eu-west. will monitor error rate post-rollback.

Support Bot: Alert: runtime-canary-rollback started by jordan at 09:24:00 UTC.

Sam (eng-sre): post-rollback telemetry (09:28): apigw 502 rate reduced to baseline, conn resets dropped to normal. host CPU stable. looks like rollback mitigated the primary signal.

Alex O.: great. immediate mitigation steps executed and customer routed to Dedicated. next: we need a short postmortem and action items to prevent recurrence. please add short bullet items and owners here by EOD.

Jordan (eng-runtime): root cause candidate: kernel path introduced a socket option/timing regression under connection churn when KV-cache eviction fires. fix plan: revert bad option + add integration test for heavy-conn churn with kv-evict. Owner: jordan. ETA: patch + canary next week (beta sprints).

Sam (eng-sre): infra/observability action: add a dashboard panel correlating `kv-cache-evict` events, `conn_reset` and `apigw-5xx` by host; add alert rule when conn_reset spike > 5/min on any host. Owner: sam. ETA: 3 days.

Niaj (infra): routing & control-plane action: add a canary gating step to prevent automatic rollout to eu-west before 24h of low-error telemetry. Owner: niaj. ETA: 5 days.

Maya CS: customer comms: send wrap-up email with timeline, what we did, and offer post-incident credits as needed. Owner: maya. ETA: today.

Li (billing): do not see quota issues; create a ledger entry for any credits we owe and run it by finance. Owner: li. ETA: tomorrow.

Alex O.: I'll own the postmortem doc and link artifacts (logs, charts, rollback diff) — will draft and share draft by EOD. Closing criteria: postmortem published + alerts added + runtime fix in dev.

Support: customer verified full recovery and accepted Dedicated fallback for now; will coordinate with their infra to move keys to Dedicated permanently if they want.

Eve (oncall): locking in next steps: weekly follow-up in incident channel to track action items. tagging owners. :checkered_flag:

Jordan (eng-runtime): quick note for postmortem: include the canary ripple timeline and the specific config diff (socket opt). will attach PR link.

Sam (eng-sre): adding one more mitigator for future: auto-fallback policy for suspicious `apigw-5xx` bursts on a per-key basis that routes to last-known-good variant (can be toggleable). Owner: sam + niaj. ETA: 2 weeks.

Alex O.: thanks everyone. I'll publish a short root-cause summary and next-steps doc in incidents folder (INC-2026-1745019999) when done. Good job on fast mitigation. :tada:
